The date GovInfo issued the package; for CHRG packages this is the (first) held date: the summary's dateIssued equals the MODS's first heldDate on 185 of 185 published transcripts (2026-10-03), and the meeting's date on 117 of 117 matched to committee_meetings.  held_date states it from the MODS itself.
When the publisher last modified the package; the merge prefers the larger value.
Digest of the extracted text, so a re-extraction that changed nothing is visible as such.
The committee-meeting event id the Congress.gov hearing record names as its associatedMeeting, which committee_meetings.event_id joins on; NULL where the hearing names none or was not looked up.
Literal witness statements in publisher order. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
Committees named by the hearing MODS. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.

The day the hearing was held, as the package's MODS states it in `<heldDate>`; NULL where the MODS states none.  A compiled volume states several (2 of 185 published transcripts, 2026-10-03; CHRG-117shrg56721 states eleven) and this is the first: it dates the package, as date_issued does, so there it is when the series began, not each session's date.  hearing_bill_links.held_date is NULL on the same volume for a different reason: a link pairs a date with a bill, and the volume pairs none.

The committee-meeting event id the package's GovInfo MODS states in `<eventId>` (the first, where it states several), which committee_meetings.event_id joins on with congress and chamber.  A second publisher's statement beside event_id, never overriding it: a consumer may fall back to it where event_id is NULL.  43 of 185 published transcripts state one, 22 where Congress.gov names none, 21 of them Senate; where both state one they agree 21 of 21 (2026-10-03), including a misassignment both make (CHRG-118hhrg63377 names 116369, another subcommittee's hearing that day), so agreement is not independent confirmation.

hearing_transcripts.subject: congress
hearing_transcripts.grain: One row per captured GovInfo hearing transcript package.

hearing_bill_links.label: Hearing-to-bill links
hearing_bill_links.summary: One row per package, bill and link source, shaped by spicy-docs.
hearing_bill_links.coverage: Sampled. Bill references that the selected hearing packages' MODS records state on their cover. It does not show bills named only in constituent records, agendas, bill actions or transcript text, and does not measure recall; agenda acquisition remains deferred.
hearing_bill_links.data_quality: mods_cover means held_on. The package measured confirmation on 19 of 20 cover pairs and 18 of 18 pairs where cover and agenda agreed. Agenda links mean noticed, not held_on: agenda-only pairs were confirmed 1 of 18, contradicted 1 and unverifiable 16. Recall is unmeasured. Only 2 of 20 sampled House hearings and 0 of 3 Senate hearings stated COVER bills; a missing row does not establish that a hearing concerned no bills. A successfully re-read cover replaces that hearing's prior links, including an empty result. Unread or refused bodies retain their prior links. held_date is the one date the hearing's MODS states. A compiled volume that states several dates has held_date NULL and every native date, in source order, in held_dates; the list does not establish that each bill was considered on each date. Before link rule d06e0bd80ca1 (2026-09-25) such a volume's links carried its first date (CHRG-117shrg56721 states eleven), and rows not re-read since keep held_dates NULL. committee_system_code is the first of its hearing's hearing_transcripts.committee_system_codes, set again every run, so a link and its hearing state one committee key.

columns.description: The CHRG package the hearing was printed as, spelled exactly as `hearing_transcripts.package_id` is, which is this table's document key.
The numbered Congress, from the package id's own grammar.
The chamber, from the package id's document-type code rather than from its first letter, the same rule `hearing_transcripts.chamber` uses.

The `authorityId` of the first `congCommittee` the package MODS names, already keyed the way `committees.system_code` is.  Half the join key a bill-side confirmation needs, and half the identity check an agenda row passed before it was written.

The day the hearing was held, where the package MODS states one distinct `heldDate`; NULL where it states none or several (a compiled volume, whose dates are held_dates).  Not the day its transcript was issued.  The other half of the confirmation join key.

The committee-meeting event id this link was reached through, so an agenda row joins `committee_meetings` and its own transcript row.  NULL on a cover row whose caller read no hearing detail: the MODS itself never states one.
`congress_bills.bill_id` for the measure, in the publisher's own type and number.  Part of the identity.

Which rule in `interpretation/hearing_bill_links.py` stated this pair, from a sealed additions-only vocabulary: `mods_cover` (the package MODS's own cover list) and `docs_house_br` (the House Committee Repository's agenda) are implemented; `daily_digest_entry`, `congress_related_items` and `front_matter_designator` are measured, named and not yet filled.  Part of the identity, because two sources naming one pair is the evidence and collapsing them would delete it; additions-only because this value is published and a rename rewrites rows already out.

What the row asserts, from the sealed vocabulary `held_on` and `noticed`.  `mods_cover` rows are `held_on`, confirmed 19 of 20 by the bill's own action list; `docs_house_br` rows are `noticed`, because an agenda states intent and an agenda-only bill is confirmed 1 of 18, contradicted 1 and unverifiable 16.

The exact string the rule read, so a wrong row is readable without the record in hand: the MODS `context` marker on a cover row, and the `BILLS-118HR188ih.pdf` file name, the `legis-num` or the `description` on an agenda row.

Every nonempty `heldDate` the package MODS states, as a Native list in document order with repetitions kept; `[]` where it states none.  A compiled volume states several, and which bill was heard on which day is not stated, so no bill is paired with a date.  NULL on a row not re-read since the column was added (`mods_cover` 002). Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.

hearing_bill_links.subject: congress
hearing_bill_links.grain: One row per bill one source states a hearing was held on or noticed for: the pair, the source that stated it, and the committee-and-date key the statement was checked against.

cbo_cost_estimates.label: CBO cost-estimate publication index
cbo_cost_estimates.summary: One row per bill and CBO publication, using build_bill_family's own cbo_cost_estimates output and spicy-docs' feed builder, merged by `merge_cbo_cost_estimates`: where both routes state one bill and publication, the BILLSTATUS row stands. One publication can stand under two bills, and both rows publish.
cbo_cost_estimates.coverage: Sampled: the estimates CBO lists for the bills the bill family has read, from the 108th Congress on, from two routes merged: each bill's BILLSTATUS record (`source` `billstatus_bulk`) and CBO's own per-Congress feed (`cbo_feed`), read once by every run for each Congress it is scoped to. BILLSTATUS states no estimate for the 112th and 113th, so theirs come from the feed alone; elsewhere the feed adds only what no BILLSTATUS record lists, such as the Recovery Act, H.R. 3200 and the ACA. A Congress no scoped run has read the feed of yet holds its BILLSTATUS estimates only. A feed item that names no bill has no row here (`cbo_feed_items` lists it): CBO's weekly estimates of the bills the House takes up under suspension of the rules, a committee's reconciliation recommendations, and an estimate CBO files under no bill number. A bill passed under suspension can be scored in such a weekly estimate first or only, so its first row here does not date CBO's first estimate of it. An absent estimate does not mean CBO never scored a bill. No CBO.gov body is requested.
cbo_cost_estimates.data_quality: The bill's cbo_cost_estimates_outcome distinguishes an absent or empty element, an unexpected shape, and populated estimates. An empty index does not establish that CBO never scored the bill. Report citations are the bill's list, not proof that each publication is reprinted in each report; the report's recital gate is evaluated separately. A feed row carries its bill's own BILLSTATUS report citations, read by the same run or carried from the bill's published rows, and NULL where neither names them. A successfully evaluated bill replaces its prior BILLSTATUS rows, including when the list is absent or empty; an unexpected list shape retains prior rows until a successful read can establish the current relationships. A feed read replaces its Congress's prior feed rows, so an item CBO withdraws or re-files leaves, and a feed that cannot be read keeps them. `found_by` says how each row names its bill; the rows published before it take `billstatus` in a one-time backfill. `title_bill_id` is the bill the estimate's title leads with: where it differs from `bill_id` (7 of the 12,732 BILLSTATUS rows on 2026-09-29), `bill_id` is a numbering error as published and `title_bill_id` the bill scored. A title leading with a public law reads through the published `laws` table, which held the 119th Congress alone on 2026-09-29, so such a title of an earlier Congress leaves `title_bill_id` NULL and a blank feed item titled by an earlier law has no row (110th P.L. 110-50 and 112th P.L. 112-8). CBO's 119th-Congress feed, read 2026-10-03, holds 53 items that name no bill and have no row, 48 of them weekly suspension estimates. 23 of them are among the feed's 674 items dated 2026: 21 suspension estimates, 62413 (reconciliation recommendations of the Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs committee) and 62643 (the Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2027).

columns.description: The bill the source attached this estimate to, as published, keyed the way congress_bills.bill_id is: the bill whose BILLSTATUS record lists it (`billstatus_bulk`), or the bill CBO's feed item names by Bill_Number, by a bare-number Bill_Number and the title's leading citation of that number, or, where Bill_Number is empty, by the citation its title leads with or by the bill the host's laws table says enacted the law it leads with (`cbo_feed`; found_by says which).  Where title_bill_id differs, this number is wrong and title_bill_id names the bill the estimate scores.
The numbered Congress the bill belongs to.
Lowercase publisher bill or resolution type (hr, s, hjres...).
The measure's number within its Congress and type.

CBO's own publication number, parsed from the stated url by the `cbo_publication_url` rule and part of this row's identity.  This is the key CBO's per-Congress feed also states, so that feed's own spelling of the measure, which no GovInfo route gives, joins here.  It is not unique alone: where the routes file one estimate under two bills, both rows publish -- CBO's feed files 22065, its estimate of P.L. 111-322, under the 112th's H.R. 3082 and the 111th's H.R. 3082 BILLSTATUS lists it -- and title_bill_id names the bill it scores.

The publisher's pubDate for this estimate; the merge prefers the larger value.  It is when CBO published the estimate, not when the bill acted.  A `cbo_feed` row states the feed's Date as the same instant in UTC, spelled as BILLSTATUS spells pubDate.
The estimate's title as the publisher states it, which is usually the bill's own title.

CBO's own statement of which printing it scored ("As ordered reported by the House Committee on Energy and Commerce on March 24, 2023").  The only field that distinguishes two estimates of one bill, and the field that states the stage: 826 of the 118th House's 1,062 rows begin "As ordered reported by the House C", and the tail includes Rules Committee prints, which have no committee report at all.  A `cbo_feed` row's is the feed's Description with the surrounding whitespace this package's feed parser trims, a trailing newline on many.

columns.column_type: STRUCT(estimate_index BIGINT, title VARCHAR, description VARCHAR, pub_date VARCHAR)[]
columns.description: Every other item naming this publication whose fields differ from the row's, in list order, as a Native list of objects carrying `estimate_index` and only the differing fields; `[]` when they agree or there is no other item.  In the 118th (measured 2026-09-20) 9 of the 37 restated rows differ, every one in `title` alone -- CBO re-spelling the bill's title ('Human rights' to 'Human Rights', one double-escaped ampersand).  In the 108th-111th every row carries its http twin, which differs in `url` and, on all but 11 of 4,762, in `description`, which it wraps in a p element.  The column exists so folding onto the identity drops nothing. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.

How many committee reports this bill's own BILLSTATUS names, on a `cbo_feed` row too, where the host supplies that record; NULL on a `cbo_feed` row shaped without it. Zero means this document names no report citation; it does not establish that no CRPT package exists. 883 of the 1,368 scored bills of the 118th are nonzero (64.5%), and the Senate shortfall is structural -- 155 of 395 scored Senate bills were reported without a written report.

columns.column_type: STRUCT(citation VARCHAR, congress VARCHAR, number VARCHAR, part VARCHAR, report_type VARCHAR)[]
columns.description: Every citation that bill's `<committeeReports>` states, as a Native list in publisher order (NULL where report_citation_count is), each carrying the `citation` verbatim and its parsed `congress`, `report_type` and `number` -- the three columns `committee_reports` publishes -- plus `part` where the citation names one.  A part citation has no package id under GovInfo's sealed CRPT grammar, so none is invented; the parsed parts are NULL on any citation outside the measured shape. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.

The bill this estimate's own title leads with ("H.R. 3447, a bill to extend ..."), keyed as bill_id is and read by the feed's title rule; for a title leading with a public law ("P.L. 111-322, ..."), the bill the host's laws table says enacted it, where the host supplies that map.  NULL where the title leads with no citation, cites the bill only after its start ("Senate Amendment 1183 to S. 744"), is ambiguous, or names a law the host did not map.  Where it differs from bill_id the row is a numbering error and this is the bill the estimate scores: over the 108th-119th (2026-09-28), 5 BILLSTATUS rows and 5 feed rows by bill titles -- four of CBO's own wrong numbers on both, 112 H.R. 1707 for S. 1707 on the feed, and 114 H.R. 3347 on BILLSTATUS, whose record lists CBO's estimate of H.R. 3447 -- and, with a law map, 2 more on both (P.L. 119-21's estimates filed under H. Con. Res. 14) and 1 more on the feed (P.L. 111-322 filed under the 112th's H.R. 3082, its bill's number in the 111th).  A bill citation reads in the row's own Congress, so this cannot show a link to the same number in another Congress: 115 H.R. 1422's BILLSTATUS lists 52538, CBO's estimate of the 113th's H.R. 1422, and this reads 115-hr-1422; that pub_date, 2013-04-22, precedes the 115th.  On a `cbo_feed` row whose found_by is `title`, `title_law` or `bill_number_title` the title chose bill_id, so the two agree by construction and the agreement proves nothing: 237 of the 108th-119th's feed rows with the host's law map, 235 without (2026-09-28).  title_bill_id_rule names the rule.

cbo_cost_estimates.subject: congress
cbo_cost_estimates.grain: One row per bill and CBO publication a source names as a cost estimate of it: the bill's own BILLSTATUS document or CBO's per-Congress feed, read for every Congress and merged, the bill's own record winning where both name one bill and publication.

cbo_feed_items.label: CBO cost-estimate feed items
cbo_feed_items.summary: One row per CBO publication as its feed lists it: the Congress, the date as `cbo_cost_estimates.pub_date` spells it, the title, link and description, and the `Bill_Number` exactly as stated (empty where CBO names no bill). Joined to `cbo_cost_estimates` on `publication_id`, the items with no estimate row are the ones naming no bill: CBO's weekly estimates of the bills the House takes up under suspension of the rules, a committee's reconciliation recommendations, and estimates filed under no number.
cbo_feed_items.coverage: Sampled: every item of CBO's keyless per-Congress cost-estimate feed for each Congress a bill-family run has read the feed of, from the 108th on, whether or not the item names a bill. A run reads each scoped Congress's feed whole and its items replace that Congress's prior items; a feed it could not read keeps them. The scheduled run reads the sitting Congress's feed; earlier Congresses fill only by a bill-family dispatch scoped to them.
cbo_feed_items.data_quality: An item that names no bill is the publisher's statement, not an extraction miss; its bills are listed only in CBO's own document, which is not requested. Measured with the spicy-docs reader over the 108th-119th feeds on 2026-10-03: 15,156 items, every one a row; 361 have no estimate row (352 name no bill, 9 are refused), 53 of them in the 119th, 48 of those suspension notices.

columns.description: CBO's own publication number, the digits of the item's Link, and this row's identity: no publication is listed twice across the 15,156 items of the 108th-119th feeds (2026-10-03).  cbo_cost_estimates.publication_id joins here, and an item with no row there is one no estimate row holds: one that names no bill (the House's weekly 'Legislation considered under suspension' notices, reconciliation titles, a continuing appropriations act; 53 in the 119th feed on 2026-10-03), a title led by a public law the host's laws table did not map, or a Bill_Number no rule maps, which the family pass refuses by name.
The numbered Congress whose feed lists the item, which a bill it names belongs to.

The item's Date as the UTC instant cbo_cost_estimates.pub_date spells it, so the two compare as text; the merge prefers the larger value.  An item whose Date names no instant is a named refusal, not a row (none in the 108th-119th feeds, 2026-10-03).
The item's Title as CBO states it, which names the bill where it names one.
The item's Link, the publication page on www.cbo.gov, exactly as stated; every measured one is walled.
The item's Description as the feed parser trims it, which states the printing scored; NULL where the element is empty, as cbo_cost_estimates.description is.

The item's Bill_Number exactly as CBO states it, `` (the empty string) where the element is empty: the feed's own statement that the item names no bill by number.  Every item of the 108th-119th feeds states the element (2026-10-03).  Unparsed here; cbo_cost_estimates.bill_id is the bill a rule reads from it, or from the title where it is empty.

cbo_feed_items.subject: congress
cbo_feed_items.grain: One row per item of CBO's keyless per-Congress cost-estimate feed, as CBO lists it, whether or not the item names a bill.

gao_decisions.label: Government Accountability Office legal decisions
gao_decisions.summary: One row per GAO legal decision page, read from GAO's own listing of what it issued by month and year. A decision is keyed on its number as GAO spells it and its page: one teaser can name several B-numbers (`B-423916.2,B-423916.3`), and one B-number can have two pages released months apart (`b-331093` and `b-331093-0`). The address of the GAO listing page each decision was read from (the former `listing_page` column) is kept in its receipt; see etl_receipts. A later walk refreshes the rows it lists; a run without one carries the table forward. A walk run given the local capture of the decision pages also reads each decision's page caption, which completes a number list the listing cut and states the decided day; a later walk without the capture keeps what a page stated. `outcome` is read again from `decision_status` on every row each run, by spicy-docs' closed table of GAO's sentences, so a new table version reaches held rows without a re-read of the walk.
gao_decisions.coverage: True range from 2009 on: every legal decision GAO's own Month in Review and Annual Index list for each year or month a finished walk of those pages read: the B-numbered decisions (bid protests, appropriations law, vacancies letters, other decisions) and the Contract Appeals Board decisions GAO numbers as dockets (`2020-02`) or `P` numbers. Federal Agency Major Rule Reports, B-numbered from April 2017, are in `gao_reports`, not here. Entries GAO gives no number are left out. A year or month the walk has not finished adds nothing, and a month with no listed decision adds nothing either; this table does not record which case a missing month is. A walk reads a year's listing (`month-in-review/2025?page=N`) or a month's (`month-in-review/2026/August`), as its scopes name, and the held rows came from year scopes for 2009-2025 and month scopes for 2026, so one listing page can span several months and `listing_page` names a scope, not a month. A month inside a year scope read, or before the newest month scope read, with no rows is a publisher zero (October 2025, when GAO was closed by the lapse in appropriations, is one); a month after the newest month scope is unread.
gao_decisions.data_quality:
`released_date` is when GAO released the decision, not when it decided it; `decided_date` is that day, from the Date line of the decision page's caption, so a count by one differs from a count by the other: over the 6,361 pages captured on 2026-10-03 whose caption read, the release came a median 7 days after the decision (1,294 the same day, 219 more than 90 days after; appropriations decisions a median 0), and 24 pages state a release before the decision, as GAO published them. `decided_date` is NULL, and `b_numbers` and `b_numbers_truncated` are the listing's, where no page was read: on 2026-10-03, 2 pages could not be captured, 247 print no caption (a letter, a report, a decision posted without its text) and 6 refuse for a number GAO mistyped on the page or in the listing; that run's journal names each refused page with its reason. `b_numbers_truncated` `true` is a list still cut, as B-412940's 22 listed numbers are (its page carries no decision text). Apply `html.unescape` when matching a `title`. `outcome` is NULL where GAO's listing states no status sentence for a decision, and where it states one spicy-docs' table leaves unmapped (a cost recommendation, an advisory or appropriations opinion and the like); each run's journal counts both.
GAO's own bid protest statistics, in its annual reports to Congress, are not a count of these rows: GAO counts docket numbers (B-numbers) as cases, not decision pages or procurements, per fiscal year, and takes its sustain rate over merit decisions (sustained plus denied). Here a row is one decision page, which can carry several B-numbers, dated by its release. The annual reports are rows of `gao_reports` (`GAO Bid Protest Annual Report to Congress for Fiscal Year …`) with title, date, link and at most a short abstract: their figures are not held. `decision_type` is GAO's label as its listing states it, not a check: GAO also labels a few reports `Bid Protest Decision` (B-423717, its response to section 885 of the FY2025 NDAA, and B-401197, a report to Congress on defense bid protests).

columns.description: The decision's number as GAO's listing spells it, suffixes and all (`B-424129.2`, `B-423916.2,B-423916.3`, `B-235577.2-O.M.`, a docket `2020-02`). With `url`, the key.

Native list of the decision's B-numbers: the ones its page's File line states where the page was read, else the ones in `decision_number`, split on commas and semicolons. GAO's listing cuts a few long lists, ending them `et al` or where its number field is full, and a fragment it cut mid-number is left out; b_numbers_truncated says where the list here is still the cut one. `[]` for a docket- or P-numbered decision. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.

GAO's label for the page as its listing states it: `Bid Protest Decision`, `Appropriations Decision`, `Legal Other Decision` and the like. A label, not a check: GAO also labels a few reports and letters `Bid Protest Decision` (B-423717, B-401197).
The decision's heading as GAO's listing states it: the protester or the question decided. GAO double-escapes some headings, so a few keep `—`, `—` or `&` literally.
Native list of GAO's headings the decision was listed under, in listed order. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
The decision's gao.gov page, as the listing links it (percent-encoded where GAO encodes it). With `decision_number`, the key.

The listing's Publicly Released date (its Published date where it states no release), as an ISO date: when GAO released the decision, not when it decided it (B-424477: decided 2026-08-07, released 2026-08-28). A count by fiscal year counts releases.

The day GAO decided the decision, from the Date line of its page's caption, as an ISO date; NULL where no page was read or the page prints no caption (a letter, a report, a decision GAO posts only as a PDF). GAO releases a decision after deciding it, often days later (B-424477: decided 2026-08-07, released 2026-08-28), so a count by decided_date and one by released_date differ.
GAO's outcome sentence for the decision as its listing states it, word for word with HTML whitespace collapsed (`We deny the protest.`); NULL where the listing states none.

The outcome decision_status states, read by a closed table of GAO's exact sentences: `sustained`, `sustained_in_part`, `denied`, `dismissed`, `denied_in_part_dismissed_in_part`, or `request` where the sentence decides only a request (reconsideration, costs, reimbursement, dismissal); a sentence deciding the protest and a request reads the protest's outcome. NULL where no sentence is stated or the table does not read it (an advisory opinion, an appropriations opinion, a wording GAO wrote after the table was made): never a guess.

`true` where GAO's listing cut the decision's numbers -- the list ends `et al` or in a separator, or fills the listing's number field (64 characters for decisions released 2009-2011, 252 from 2012) -- and no decision page has completed it, so b_numbers holds only what the listing names; `false` otherwise.

gao_decisions.subject: oversight
gao_decisions.grain: One row per legal decision page GAO's own Month in Review or Annual Index lists with a number: every B-numbered decision and every docket- or P-numbered other. Federal Agency Major Rule Reports, B-numbered from April 2017, are products, not rows here.

laws.label: Enacted laws
laws.summary: One row per enacted law the Congress.gov law list route states, with the Statutes at Large citation from the law's own PLAW USLM file where captured. Keyed on the law's Congress, type and number, not on the bill; `bill_id` is the foreign key to `congress_bills`, whose `statutes_at_large_cite` the host fills from this table at that table's merge.
laws.coverage: Sampled. Every law the Congress.gov law route lists for the scoped Congresses (the current one by default), walked whole each run; the PLAW USLM citation is added per law, newest first, under a per-run cap. A steady-state run is meant to ask only about laws whose list row moved or whose PLAW the bulk folder had not yet served.
laws.data_quality:
`statutes_at_large_cite` is set when `uslm_outcome` is `captured`; read every NULL through `uslm_outcome` and `uslm_reason`. `unavailable` (reason `source_unavailable`) is the publisher's own lag, a `404` from the exact PLAW locator: on 2026-09-19 the route listed 108 laws and the PLAW bulk folder held 104, the four newest (119-103, 119-104, 119-109, 119-110) absent; each is retried every run until the folder serves it.
`captured_partial` is a validated USLM file that states no Statutes at Large citation (reason `statutes_citation_not_stated`): the two private laws of the 119th (`PLAW-119pvtl1`, `PLAW-119pvtl2`), whose own `citableAs` values are kept in `uslm_citable_as`. Until reader rule `laws-uslm-v2` (2026-09-25) the contract refused those two files and their rows said `not_requested`, although both were requested and served. `captured_refused` keeps the digest of a `200` body the reader refused, either another law's file (`native_identity_refused`) or not native USLM at all, such as an HTML page (`native_shape_refused`), and none of its unvalidated fields. `request_failed` is an attempted read that established nothing, a transport failure included; it is never published as `unavailable`. `not_requested` means only that no request was made, which the per-run cap decides.
A validated row with parsed text is read again when its listing or metadata/text reader changes, or its matching section output is missing. A failed later attempt preserves its prior metadata and parsed sections. `law_text_outcome` distinguishes unread, parsed and refused text; an unavailable XML file does not mean the law has no provisions. Join `law_sections` on `law_id` for native sections. `law_body_remainder` retains main-body text outside those sections, including appropriation blocks; it is NULL unless parsed and may be an empty string on success. The section rows and remainder are printed law text, not consolidated current law. A publisher-refused Table III read is journaled `table3-bulk-refused` with reason `access-refused`, and the laws family publishes without the Table III rows that read would have added. `statutes_at_large_volume` follows the session that cleared the bill, not the year the law was approved: 119-69 and 119-71 to 119-73, approved in January 2026 on bills cleared in December 2025, are in volume 139, and 119-70 and 119-74 on are in volume 140. `statutes_at_large_last_page` comes with reader `laws-uslm-v3` (2026-10-03), so a row read under an earlier reader holds NULL there, which means not read, until the next laws run reads its PLAW again. `resolve_document_citations` resolves a Statutes citation to a page inside a law's range to that law and says the match is by range (`match_basis`); a law with no last page is matched by its first page only.

columns.description: Natural key: congress, law_type and number joined with hyphens.
The numbered Congress that enacted the law.
`public` or `private`: the publisher's Public Law or Private Law folded onto the spelling the PLAW USLM publicPrivate field uses, so the list route, the bulk folder and the USLM file share one key.
The law's number within its Congress and type, without the Congress prefix.
The publisher's own spelling of the number, Congress prefix included.
The publisher's laws[].type exactly as spelled (Public Law or Private Law).
The GovInfo PLAW package id by the measured bulk-file rule: `PLAW-` plus congress, publ or pvtl, and number.
Natural key of the measure this law enacted, as congress_bills keys it.
The enacted measure's type, lowercased as the bill tables spell it.
The enacted measure's number.
The measure's title as the list route states it.

law_sections.label: Published law sections
law_sections.summary: One row per native section occurrence in a published law's main body. These are the law's own words, including amendment instructions, not a consolidated statement of current law. Section numbers and publisher IDs can repeat or be absent; (law_id, seq) identifies each occurrence and native_path locates it in the source XML. is_quoted marks sections inside quotedContent; parent_seq alone does not imply a quotation. Body excludes its own number and heading, print furniture, and nested sections' text; query the child rows as well. laws.law_body_remainder retains text outside all numbered sections, including appropriation blocks. Hierarchy retains the source context. Boolean and numeric observations use native types.

Join law_id to laws.law_id, then laws.bill_id to congress_bills.bill_id. A missing section row does not establish that the law has no text: check law_text_outcome and law_section_count in laws. Coverage follows successfully read XML, not all enacted laws. PDF-only sources are outside this reader.

law_code_sections.label: Law classifications by Congress
law_code_sections.summary: One row per line of an OLRC per-Congress classification table: a U.S. Code place one public law section touched, with the Statutes at Large page and the publisher's action word.
law_code_sections.coverage: Sampled. Every row of each public-law-order table the OLRC classification index links for a scoped Congress, read whole every run and replacing that session's rows. The index links the current Congress's session tables only.
law_code_sections.data_quality: A row is its position on the page (`seq`), because one line can repeat; a page read this run replaces every prior row for its Congress and session, so a line the publisher removed does not linger under a position it no longer holds. A session not read keeps its rows, and `observed_at` says when they were read. On 2026-10-02 and -03 OLRC answered its classification pages with a maintenance page and status 200, which the reader refuses rather than reading as an empty table. A refused page, or a 401/403, is journaled as `classification-refused` with its URL, status and time, and the nightly `scripts/check_source_refusals.py` fails while the current laws generation holds one; a 401/403 that leaves no session table read also fails the laws run after it publishes. A transport failure is only retried on the next run. Only the public-law order is read: the code-order twin holds the same lines under positions that would collide with these. A Congress the index does not link — every Congress but the current one — gets no rows here; `table3_records` is the historical view. `action` is the page's column 3 verbatim, NULL where the page left it blank, which its legend reads as amended. `usc_section_key` is `usc_section` folded for joins (trimmed, lower-cased, every dash spelling an ASCII hyphen), because case carries no identity in the Code and a join on the printed letter misses the upper-case spellings (decision 30, `docs/research/fork-delivery-decisions-2026-09-22.md`). Every laws run derives `usc_section_key` and `usc_place` again on every row from its stored `usc_section` and `action`, so a session not read keeps current ones; a row meets its `table3_records` record on `law_number` (its `act_key`), title, key and place. A law can be classified in the session table after the one its number suggests (119-70 is in the session-2 table, whose caption names it); filter by `law_id`, not by `session`, and `stated_laws` carries each table's caption.

Tokens combine (`nt new`: a new note). A transfer prints as `tr fr <title>/<section>` (from that section) or `tr to <title>/<section>` (to it), the legend's `fr` and `to`. table3_records.label: Table III records
table3_records.summary: One row per classification record of one public law in OLRC's Table III: which U.S. Code place each section of the law went to, as Table III's bulk file states it.
table3_records.coverage: Window, complete for the Congresses read: every public law Table III holds for each Congress the laws table holds, plus the scoped ones, derived from OLRC's Table III bulk file on each run, so a Congress keeps its rows current after it leaves the laws scope while Table III catches up. The file holds the whole table back to 1789; other Congresses, private laws and pre-1957 session-law chapters are not derived.
table3_records.data_quality:
Table III holds an act only once OLRC has classified it, and lags enactment: on 2026-09-26 it was current through 119-73, a law of 2026-01-23, while the law route reached 119-111. `release_point` says how current the file was. Its file at release point 119-73 also has no record of 119-70, a second-session law `law_code_sections` classifies (OLRC's gap, not a reading error).
Since 2026-09-26 the rows come from the bulk file (`fulldump@<release point>.xml`) instead of one page per act. The file splits an act's records about ten to an `<act>` fragment. An act's rows are its fragments' records in the file's order, and `seq` is a record's position in its act, as on the page; the file's own `sequence` attribute repeats within 70 acts, so it is not used. Each fragment states its own Congress, date and Statutes volume, and a record carries its fragment's volume where it states a page. Replayed against the 2,981 rows the pages had published, every row keeps its position, act section, Statutes page and volume, Code title and section, status and release point. The file also holds 119-30 and 119-53, whose pages the page walk never reached. Four act-level columns now carry the file's spelling instead of the page's: `stated_key` `119-37` (page `119–37`), `congress` `119` (`119th Cong.`), `act_date` `2025-11-12` (`Nov. 12, 2025`) and `statutes_at_large_volume` `139` (`139 Stat.`).
OLRC states no Last-Modified, ETag or Content-Length for the zip, so each run fetches it; it was byte-identical on 2026-09-14 and 2026-09-26 at the same release point. Each Congress keeps a checkpoint in the file's metadata: the derivation rule with a digest of SpicyDocs' code (not its release string, so a version-only release derives nothing), the member's digest and release point, and each act's shaped-row digest. While all match, nothing is derived. Otherwise every scoped act is derived again, and only an act whose rows changed is published, its whole row set replaced.
Table III only grows: across the eight consecutive releases from 116-150 (2020-07) to 119-73, archived by the Wayback Machine, no act was ever dropped (receipt `table3-bulk-2026-09-26/wayback/`). So a held act the file no longer lists loses its rows only when the release point advances, at most one act a release, and the removal is journaled as `rows-retired` for qualification to reconcile. A file whose release point is older than the one published, that drops an act without advancing, or that drops more than one is refused, and so is a file the reader refuses outright: the member has been renamed twice since 2020. A refused read publishes nothing for this table and keeps every checkpoint, while `laws` and `law_code_sections` publish as usual. The build journals it as `table3-bulk-refused`, and the nightly `scripts/check_source_refusals.py` fails while the current laws generation holds one, so the table cannot stop updating in silence. A transport failure is only retried on the next run. `usc_section_key` is the bare section folded for joins (trimmed, lower-cased, every dash spelling an ASCII hyphen), because case carries no identity in the Code and Table III itself prints some sections both ways (decision 30, `docs/research/fork-delivery-decisions-2026-09-22.md`); the note or preceding words Table III prints inside `usc_section` are in `usc_place` (until 2026-10-03 they stayed in the key, on 1,121 of 2,983 rows). Every laws run derives both again on every row from its stored `usc_section`, so held rows need no read of the file for them.

Read from the section as Table III prints it (`1101 nt`, `prec. 1071`, `nt. prec. 791`) and from the head of law_code_sections.action (`nt new`, `prec`, `nt prec new`), by schemas.law_tables.usc_section_place. committees.label: Committees
committees.summary: One row per committee or subcommittee of any Congress the Congress.gov committee list route states, keyed on the publisher's `systemCode`, with the detail record's history, subcommittees, parent and currency folded on where captured.
committees.coverage: Sampled. Since 2026-09-26 the Congress.gov committee route is walked whole with no Congress: every committee of every Congress the publisher records, because `committee_meetings` keeps the previous Congress and `bill_committees` reaches the 108th. The committee detail is folded onto each row under a per-run cap, newest `update_date` first; a committee whose detail was captured is re-read only when its list row's `update_date` moves. Receipt `committee-fixes-2026-09-26/3-rosters-118/`.
committees.data_quality: The route over-declares: on 2026-09-19 `committee/119` declared 238 and served 236 on its one terminal page with no continuation. The reader's terminal-page count refusal is the one refusal this rollup reads past, publishing what the publisher served with both numbers in the run log; every other walk refusal fails the run. `detail_captured` says whether the detail's columns are the publisher's or NULL; where the detail was captured, its `subcommittees` are the row's, an empty list included. The detail's counts (`bill_count` and the rest) are that day's statement, dated by `detail_update_date`. Rows are committees of every Congress: filter `is_current` for today's. 95 historical committees are keyed on their Library of Congress name-authority id (`n79043125`, the Senate's Indian Affairs, 1820-1946), which their history states as `locLinkedDataId`; none is current. A code the detail route cannot address is a list row with `detail_captured` false.

committee_assignments.label: Committee assignments
committee_assignments.summary: One row per member per committee or subcommittee seat a chamber roster file lists today, from the House Clerk's MemberData.xml and the Senate's cvc_member_data.xml.
committee_assignments.coverage: Sampled. Today's seats: the House Clerk's and the Senate's committee files are captured whole each run, for the current Congress only, and each capture replaces its chamber's rows for that Congress; an earlier Congress keeps its last capture. Vacant and placeholder seats appear as the Clerk's file states them.
committee_assignments.data_quality: A row is a seat the file listed on its `file_date`: a seat the file no longer lists is gone on the next capture. The House file states its Congress and the reader proves it; the Senate file states none, so its rows carry the caller's Congress with `congress_basis` = `caller`. A House vacancy has no member and no row, and a seated member whose only assignment is the file's `<committee rank=""/>` placeholder has none either (nine placeholders on 2026-09-19). Only a file captured this run replaces its chamber's rows; a chamber whose file was not established keeps its prior rows. House `system_code` derives its prefix from the native committee type and parent context; `committee_code` preserves the literal source identifier. Join matching `system_code` values to `committees` and `bioguide_id` to `members`. Rows whose `system_code` matches no committee stay listed and are never matched by name (the Joint Economic Committee has three Congress.gov codes). On 2026-09-23 that is 28 rows: 25 House seats on the Clerk's four joint committees (`EC00`, `IT00`, `JL00`, `JP00`, typed `joint` in the Clerk file with no Congress.gov code), and three Senate seats on `JSIK00`, the 2024 inaugural committee, which Congress.gov does not list in any Congress.

federal_register.label: Federal Register documents
federal_register.summary: One row per dated Federal Register record, keyed by (`document_number`, `publication_date`), ingested from the federalregister.gov REST API by `build_federal_register`. The authoritative rule-publication record — proposed rules, final rules, and notices — complementary to the regulations.gov `dockets`/`documents` view. `regulation_id_numbers` (RIN) and `cfr_references` are the join keys to the Unified Agenda and the CFR.
federal_register.coverage: True range: dated records published from 1994-01-03 on, the whole span the API serves.
federal_register.data_quality: Document numbers are not globally unique: `00-111` names different records on 2000-01-14 and 2000-01-18. Current merging preserves both dates and replaces only the same dated record on a later successful fetch. This code correction does not restore historical records already lost from published files; those require a pinned historical replay and publication. A number-only source reference remains ambiguous when its input generation supplies multiple dated candidates. One RIN, docket and title can cover a rule and its later corrections, effective-date delays and confirmations, all typed `Rule` since 2008 with `subtype` NULL, so a RIN or title match picks a document family, not a document; `action` tells them apart (`Final rule; correction.`) where the Register states one. The API lists no RIN on a large share of `Rule` documents every year, some of which state one in the printed text or inside `docket_ids`. A row not read since the Register's regulations.gov link and `action` were first requested (2026-10-03) is NULL in all nine of those columns, which means not read: test `regulations_dot_gov_info_json`, which a row read since holds as `'{}'` at least. The scheduled run re-reads the last 120 days, so a relayed comment count follows the Register's own checks to about the comment period's close.

Since 2008 a correction, an effective-date delay or a confirmation of a rule is itself typed `Rule` and shares the rule's RIN, docket and title; subtype is NULL on recent records, so tell them apart by `action`.
The date the document was published, canonical YYYY-MM-DD.

house_communications.label: House executive communications
house_communications.summary: One row per House executive communication, as the Congress.gov house-communication list and detail routes state it, keyed on the publisher's own address. The regulatory bridge: `is_rulemaking`, the cited `legal_authority`, the committee referral, the matching House requirement and the RIN read from `report_nature`. A Federal Register RIN join must unnest `regulation_id_numbers` (the scalar `federal_register.rin` is the first value only) and retain number plus publication date. The Register API lists no RIN on many `Rule` documents, including some whose printed text states one, and sometimes prints the RIN inside `docket_ids`, so a RIN join misses those and can land on a correction or effective-date notice that shares the rule's RIN, docket and title; `federal_register.action` tells such a notice from its rule.
house_communications.coverage: Window: the sitting Congress (the 119th), every communication the Congress.gov house-communication list declares for each type (`ec`, `ml`, `pm`, `pt`), the list walked whole each run and refused short of the publisher's declared total, with every detail read. A later run reads new details newest first under its per-run cap, so a row it has not reached is list-only (`detail_read` false), not absent. The output ledger records the declared counts beside what is held.
house_communications.data_quality: A row whose `detail_read` is `false` is list-only: its detail has not been read yet (not reached under the cap, or refused), and every detail-only column is NULL with it, including the scalar and occurrence RIN columns, because the rule was not run. A read detail's list is `[]` where the detail states an empty one and NULL where it states none. Rows read before spicy-docs 0.54.0 spelled both `[]`; each such row is read once more (817 on 2026-10-03, one run). The RIN is an interpretation: `rin_rule` names the rule that fired (`report_nature_rin_label/2`) or `unmatched`, and `rin_matched_text` is the exact text, so a false positive is readable from the row. Every run derives the four RIN columns of each read row again from its retained `report_nature`, re-read or not, so no row keeps an earlier SpicyDocs' scalar or rule name. The rows the `rin_rule` column note says name `report_nature_rin_label` last only until this table's first run under SpicyDocs 0.50.1: after it, no row names the old rule. The publisher repeats a record across a page boundary; the table holds each identity once. The shared pooled list reader must settle each query by distinct identity before any output is replaced. Every existing publisher row receives source_route=congress-gov-detail. The four Record evidence columns remain NULL until the separate Record backfill, one GovInfo request per entry, is acquired in the next rollup. In that future reconstruction submitting_official and submitting_agency must both remain NULL: held-out precision was 85.3% and 88.4%, below the declared 90% gate. The original sentence stays in record_entry_text.

committee_meetings.label: Committee meetings
committee_meetings.summary: One row per scheduled committee meeting, as the Congress.gov committee-meeting list and detail routes state it, keyed `(congress, chamber, event_id)`. The detail carries the hearing transcript jackets (`hearing_transcripts` joins on `event_id`), the related bills, the witnesses and every document URL.
committee_meetings.coverage: Sampled, and accumulating. Each run walks the current Congress's whole `committee-meeting` list, and the previous Congress's from the day before its newest held `updateDate` (or its oldest unread row), and reads the detail of every meeting the table does not yet hold, newest `updateDate` first, at most 1,000 a run; a meeting whose detail is unread or refused has its list fields only. The previous Congress stays in scope because its meetings change when GovInfo prints their transcripts, and hearing transcripts have named meetings the table lacked (receipt `join-gaps-2026-09-26/f/`).
committee_meetings.data_quality:
A row whose `detail_read` is `false` is list-only: its detail has not been read yet, and every detail-only column is NULL with it. A read detail's list is `[]` where the detail states an empty one and NULL where it states none. Rows read before spicy-docs 0.54.0 spelled both `[]`; each such row is read once more, after a run's own reads and under its cap of 1,000, and until then its `[]` can mean either. Event ids are keyed with their chamber because their uniqueness across chambers is unmeasured (spicy-docs' contract note); the 119th's House and Senate event ids come from different ranges, so an id alone does not say which chamber. The publisher's witness entries can repeat within one meeting, so count people by name, not entries.
**Related bills.** Congress.gov often leaves the related bills off a markup's detail, so `bill_ids_json` names none; the meeting's documents usually still name them, in a `meeting_documents_json` entry whose `documentType` is `Bills and Resolutions`. A bill named only in a meeting document is not in `bill_ids_json`.
**A meeting can carry no committee**: `committee_system_code` and `committees_json` are NULL where the detail names none (Senate Finance's nominations meeting of 2026-07-23, event 338678), so a filter on the committee misses it; search `title` as well. **`meeting_status` is Congress.gov's and can lag**: a hearing the committee rescheduled can stay `Scheduled` under its first date (Senate Finance's trade-agenda hearing, event 338326 on 2026-04-23, which the committee lists as rescheduled to July, event 338681).
**Senate and NoChamber meetings list no witnesses here.** Congress.gov's committee-meeting detail, the route this table reads, has no `witnesses` element for those chambers (retained detail `119/nochamber/338692`), so their witness lists are `[]` or NULL: the route stated none, not that the meeting had none. For a printed hearing, `hearing_transcripts.witnesses_json` lists the witnesses GovInfo's MODS names (CHRG-119shrg64653 names four). A transcript reaches its meeting by `event_id`, or by `mods_event_id` where `event_id` is NULL, with `congress` and `chamber`; most Senate transcripts name no meeting either way, so most Senate meetings have no witness list from either source.
The publisher's `NoChamber` value is stored as `nochamber`, matching its detail address and preserving the existing row identity. It is neither NULL nor an inferred `joint` chamber. The source reader accepts that address, so previously list-only rows can fill at an unchanged timestamp. Retained meeting `119/nochamber/338692` names the Helsinki Commission; the September 24 committee-meetings audit retains its list row and served detail.

The detail's section names give `chambers`, the legislative-day calendar (which chambers sat), and the stem of the whole-issue link for part 1 gives the GovInfo CREC `package_id` (`entire_issue_url_stem/2`). The volume is the year minus 1854 (volume 172 is 2026).
record_issues.coverage: Sampled, and accumulating. Each run walks the whole `daily-congressional-record/{volume}` list for each session volume of the Congresses in scope and reads the detail of every issue the table does not yet hold, newest `updateDate` first, up to 1,000 a run, so at the 119th's size one run completes it.
record_issues.data_quality: A row whose `detail_read` is `false` is list-only: its detail has not been read yet, so `chambers`, `package_id` and every other detail-only column are NULL with it. A read detail with no chamber section (a Daily Digest only) states an empty `chambers`, distinct from NULL. The rule before 2026-09-29 read the first whole-issue link listed, and an issue printed in several books lists a later book's `-bk{N}` link first on 7 of 368 held rows, which GovInfo holds no package under; a one-time rebuild re-reads every held row's own `entire_issue` under the new rule.

house_activity_reports.label: Committee activity reports (House and Senate)
house_activity_reports.summary: One row per captured end-of-Congress committee activity report package, House or Senate (the table's name predates its Senate rows; the package id's `hrpt`/`srpt` says which), with what its print adds to its own MODS index. Joins `document_citations` on `package_id` = `document_key` and `text_sha256`.
house_activity_reports.coverage: Sampled. House committee activity reports: CRPT packages from the 2023-01-01 issue floor whose titles name activity under the shared title rule. Not an earlier-archive census.
house_activity_reports.data_quality: **The MODS is authoritative for bills, laws and Code sections, and this table's own columns say so.** Read at full page depth across the eight reports spicy-docs sampled, the print named 0 of 1,406 bills, 0 of 174 public laws, 0 of 37 U.S. Code sections and 0 of 7 Statutes at Large pages that the package MODS does not already state — so `distinct_bills_beyond_index`, `distinct_laws_beyond_index` and `distinct_usc_sections_beyond_index` are near zero, and a nonzero one is worth reading the evidence span for rather than taking as new yield. Measured here 2026-09-20 over **41** reports rather than eight, "zero" is very nearly right and not exactly right: 7 print-only bills of 7,686 distinct, 5 print-only laws of 990, and 6 print-only Code sections. The one apparent survivor, `188-11`, was the print's own misprint of `118-11`. What the print does add is committees beyond the submitting one (27 resolved codes), 87 RINs, 38 agency dockets and 5 GAO product ids. **Except for the Congress of a Senate report's bills.** A Senate committee files its report early in the following Congress, and GovInfo stamps the MODS's bills with that filing Congress; printed bills are keyed in `covered_congress`, the Congress the report itself states, so on a Senate report `bills_congress_mismatch` and `distinct_bills_beyond_index` count the MODS's wrong Congress, not new yield (2026-09-26 drift audit: the eight Senate reports on the 117th had published 1,915 citations under 118th-Congress bills before the fix). **And for a House report's bills printed under a Congress subheading.** CRPT-117hrpt705 and -118hrpt974 print a predecessor bill's history under `116th Congress` or `117th Congress` inside the current bill's entry, and -118hrpt967 heads each Congress of its committee history, 107th to 118th, the same way; since spicy-docs `bill_number` 004 those bills are keyed in the subheading's Congress until the next entry, while the MODS stamps them with the filing one, so `bills_congress_mismatch` and `distinct_bills_beyond_index` count them (45 on -117hrpt705, 225 on -118hrpt967; replay receipt `print-subheading-2026-09-26/`). Since `bill_number` 005 a bill the print sets its own Congress beside (`H.R. 6752, 115th Cong.`, `S. Res. 116, 112th Congress`) takes that one ahead of any subheading, and those count the same way (38 citations over the 40 reports; receipt `print-inline-congress-2026-09-26/`). A committee name both chambers hold (`Committee on the Judiciary`, `on the Budget`, `on Veterans' Affairs`, `on Armed Services`, `on Appropriations`) resolves to the chamber of the report's own committee, read off the package id; before 2026-09-26 the House won every such name, and the Senate reports published 1,746 House codes for their own committees, 1,718 of them `hsju00`. A chamber the print names before a committee (`Senate Committee on Armed Services`) selects that chamber's committees instead (76 rows moved, 24 of them `hshm00` to `ssga00`). **Limit:** 7 bare committee names in Senate reports reach a name only the House roster holds and keep the House's code, because the print names no chamber: 5 `hshm00` (a wrapped `Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs`, or its `Committee on Home-` fragment) and 2 `hsso00` (`Select Committee on Ethics`). Read them as ambiguous, not as House committees. Receipt: `fix-print-citations-2026-09-26/replay-qualified.json`. `committees_unresolved` is **a floor, not a defect count**: the Senate `cvc` roster states only the committees its listed senators sit on, so a name it does not reach stays unresolved rather than being guessed. `stated_page_count` is the publisher's own `pages` field and is never re-derived from the bytes; `pages_read` is what the extraction saw, and the two are reported separately on purpose (CRPT-118hrpt965 states 282 and a 60-page read saw 60). `submitted_by_bioguide_id` is NULL where the publisher states the member without an id, which CRPT-118hrpt965 does.

How many distinct bill keys the print names, by the shared citation rules.  A floor, not a total: it counts what pages_read reached, and the MODS is the authoritative list.  A key carries `covered_congress`, because a print mostly writes `H.R. 7806` with no Congress beside it, unless the print states the bill's own: set right after it (`H.R. 6752, 115th Cong.`), else in a Congress subheading over it (`116th Congress`), which it takes instead; where the report states none, these are the printed forms, unresolved.

Nonzero on a House report counts the bills the print keys in an earlier Congress -- beside the bill or in a subheading over it -- which the MODS stamps with the filing one, and any measure of another Congress the print names without saying so, whose row's `bill_id` is then wrong. How many of those the MODS does not already state: 0 of 37 across all eight sampled reports at full page depth.  This is the correction that removed U.S. Code sections from the family's claimed new yield; the kinds that survive are committees, RINs, agency dockets and GAO ids.

The Congress the report says it reports on, read from its own words -- the index title, else the print's cover, else its first five pages, and `covered_congress_source` says which -- and the Congress a printed bill key is built in where the print states no other for it.  Beside `congress` rather than replacing it: the two differ on every Senate report, which is filed early in the following Congress (CRPT-118srpt99 reports on the 117th).  NULL where the report states no Congress, or where the first source stating one states several; its printed bills the print states no Congress for then stay unresolved rather than being stamped with a guess.

budget_volumes.label: President's budget volumes
budget_volumes.summary: One row per published volume of the President's budget, with what its print adds to its own MODS index. Thirteen measured package parts are accepted; only volumes offering a supported package-root body yield rows.
budget_volumes.coverage: Sampled. BUDGET packages from the 2023-01-01 issue floor whose root PDF follows the provider's thirteen-part grammar, read under a per-run package cap. TAB, DB, CLIMATE and LRB have no root PDF; no granule route is attempted.
budget_volumes.data_quality:
**The bill counts are congress-blind and are not join keys.** A BUDGET package states no Congress anywhere — not in its id, not in its summary — so the print can only spell `HR7806` where the MODS states `119-hr-7806`. `distinct_bills` and `distinct_bills_beyond_index_congress_blind` therefore reduce **both** sides to `{bill_type}-{number}` before comparing, which is why the column carries `congress_blind` in its name; neither can join `congress_bills.bill_id`, which needs the Congress this family never states. For the same reason the per-row `stated_by_index` on a `bill_number` citation of a budget volume is **NULL, not `false`**: the comparison was not possible, and answering `false` would report a comparison nobody made. Measured across the eight volumes spicy-docs sampled at full page depth, 6 of the 8 distinct printed bills are print-only. The family's real yield is laws: **504 of 518** distinct public laws the prints name are absent from their own MODS at full page depth, against 43 of 69 at a 60-page cap. `fiscal_year` is not the issue year — `BUDGET-2026-MSR` was issued 2025-09-05 — and is stated twice, by the package id and by the MODS, which spicy-docs asserts agree. `associated_bills` is published whole because it is the only statement of this edge that carries a Congress.

**Thirteen measured parts are accepted by spicy-docs 0.24.0.** The seven additions are `OBJCLASS`, `TAB`, `DB`, `CLIMATE`, `LRB`, `CROSSCUT` and `DOD`. On one measured volume per part, `TAB`, `DB` and `CLIMATE` offer PDF only at granule stems; `LRB` offers an XLS and no supported body. A `GovInfoFormatNotOfferedError` at the package root is counted and logged as the publisher's answer, not as a failed or missing volume. No granule route is attempted: `shape_budget_volume` takes package summary/MODS and does not support a granule identity. These observations remain eligible on the next run and produce no invented document row.

The fiscal year this volume is the budget for, as the MODS states it in `field name="Fiscal Year"`, falling back to the year the package id itself carries where the MODS states none.  Not the year it was issued: BUDGET-2026-MSR was issued 2025-09-05.

Which part of the budget this volume is, in the publisher's own id spelling (`APP` for the Appendix, `MSR` for the Mid-Session Review).  The sealed vocabulary is in `sources/govinfo/bodies.py`'s package-id grammar, so a part no measurement has seen is a refusal rather than a row.
